messages:
Anya: hey team — quick design question: in the console modal where the primary CTA sits flush-right (data table actions) it feels really cramped when a toast stacks up underneath. thinking about either center-aligning the primary for confirm-like modals or switching to a stacked (vertical) layout for narrow widths. screenshot: https://figma.redwood/design/xyz :thinking: cc @Mike @Julia
Mike: stacking for narrow widths +1. center-align feels weird next to left-aligned table actions, will create visual imbalance. stacking (primary above secondary) keeps action hierarchy intact. :thumbsup:
Julia: stacking sounds fine. small token note — the current spacing token used between actions is `surface-gap-sm` (8px) which still looks tight with the toast shadow. bumping to 12px would help. also accessibility: when toast appears we need to ensure focus order isn't trapped behind the toast (keyboard users).
Kevin: agree with stacking. another option: keep left-aligned primary for full-width console modals and only center for lightweight confirm dialogs (delete/confirm). quick CSS snippet for stacked actions if helpful:
```
.modal .actions {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--space-2); /* use token */
}
```
Anya: nice — let's do: console/data modals = left-aligned; confirm dialogs = centered; responsive breakpoints stack on <480px. I'll update the Figma and add notes. also: @design-bot could you run a contrast check on the toast CTA? the visual was a bit low contrast.
design-bot: contrast-check: toast CTA label contrast ratio = 3.5:1 against current toast bg — fails AA for 14px normal text. recommendations: increase font-weight to 600 or use `text-on-surface-high` color. full report: https://internal-reports/design/contrast/1712345678
Julia: thanks — i'll add a token rename proposal: `surface-gap-sm` -> `surface-gap-compact` with new value 12 (and keep legacy alias for a cycle). will also add a11y checklist entry about toast focus management and open a PR for tokens + docs.
Mike: :thumbsup: sounds good. after PR + tiny QA pass (storybook interaction test for action order and focus), we're good to ship the layout update. who wants to own the QA checklist?
